section_summary: This section contains diplomatic despatches, monthly political reports, and Division of Far Eastern Affairs memoranda documenting Japan's internal and foreign affairs between December 1933 and February 1934. It covers Japan's domestic political landscape—notably parliamentary attacks on military budgets in the 65th Diet, the resignation of War Minister Sadao Araki and his replacement by General Senjuro Hayashi, agrarian distress, and the birth of the Crown Prince. In international affairs, the records focus on preparations and ratio demands for the upcoming 1935 naval limitation conference, the pending imperial enthronement of Pu Yi in Manchukuo, Sino-Japanese tensions following the return of Chang Hsueh-liang, negotiations over the Chinese Eastern Railway with the Soviet Union, and global trade frictions over Japanese textile and sundry exports.

subfiles.about: Monthly political and economic report on Japan for December 1933, detailing internal politics, foreign trade frictions, and diplomatic despatches sent.
subfiles.from: Embassy of the United States of America, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Covers the birth of Crown Prince Tsugu-No-Miya (Akihito) and the opening of the sixty-fifth session of the Imperial Diet amid intense debate over agrarian relief and the military budget. Reports on foreign trade frictions including German tariff concerns over Japanese exports, Japanese countermeasures against commercial discrimination, and Yosuke Matsuoka's resignation from the Seiyukai Party to campaign against party government. Details criminal proceedings relating to the May 15 and God-Sent Troops incidents, economic indicators including wholesale price movements and rising living costs, the death of former Premier Admiral Gombei Yamamoto, and nationwide communist arrests. Concludes with a comprehensive chronological list of diplomatic despatches forwarded to the Department of State throughout December 1933.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Embassy Report No. 87: Conditions in Japan During the Month of December, 1933

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum evaluating key foreign policy, economic, and political sections of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for January 1934.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Reviews Despatch 664 (January 1934): naval-conference preparations, reaction to arrested Japanese in New Jersey, cotton-industry shift to fine yarns and American cotton demand, wheat-subsidy alarm, Fukien revolt suppression, Soviet/Dutch rail and trade talks, Diet military pushback, and an Ethiopian bride search.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 664 (Monthly Report for January 1934)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting Embassy Tokyo's comprehensive monthly report on Japanese political, international, military, and economic developments for January 1934.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Transmits Embassy Tokyo's comprehensive report reviewing Japanese domestic and foreign developments during January 1934, beginning with naval ratio demands for the 1935 conference and friction surrounding Dr. Stanley Hornbeck's speech. Documents international developments including the forthcoming elevation of Pu Yi to Emperor of Manchukuo, the Indo-Japanese cotton textile agreement reached at Delhi, and European commercial maneuvers in Manchuria. Describes heated parliamentary interpellations in the Diet criticizing military expenditures and political meddling, the resignation of War Minister Sadao Araki due to illness, and his succession by General Senjuro Hayashi. Concludes with 1933 economic and trade figures, agrarian distress, the proposed government steel merger, the release of Premier Hara's assassin, and lists of despatches and telegrams sent during the month.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 664, Transmitting Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of January, 1934 (Report No. 88)

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing and evaluating Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on conditions in Japan for February 1934.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Appraises Tokyo's February political report for the Under Secretary of State, commending its comprehensive overview of Japanese domestic and foreign affairs. Details Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's efforts to curb inflammatory war rhetoric, Diet debates on Pacific spheres of influence, and naval concerns regarding American military bases in the event of withdrawal from the Philippines. Outlines Japan's rejection of existing naval ratios and its preference for bilateral talks with the United States and Great Britain, alongside continuing Russo-Japanese negotiations over fisheries and the Chinese Eastern Railway. Summarizes European diplomacy regarding Manchukuo, Netherlands East Indies textile import restrictions, and persistent Diet criticism of the army under new War Minister Senjuro Hayashi.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 699 (Monthly Report for February 1934)
subfiles.to: William Phillips, Under Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Covering diplomatic despatch transmitting Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on conditions in Japan for February 1934.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch 699 transmits Report 89, Tokyo's February 1934 monthly political report, forwarded by Grew to Hull per standing instructions, copied to Peiping, Shanghai, Mukden, Harbin, and Dairen posts, with intelligence-division endorsement stamps.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 699, Transmitting Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of February, 1934 (Report No. 89)
